## Description

A face whose area is below the squared sewing tolerance is removed entirely by the sewer with no diagnostic — the consumer sees a clean shell with one fewer face than the input. Typical fixture: an ADVANCED_FACE whose underlying PLANE references CARTESIAN_POINTs covering only a sub-micron sliver region (e.g., (0,0,0), (1e-6,0,0), (1e-6,1e-6,0), (0,1e-6,0)) — a face whose extent is below typical tolerance. Empty bound lists may also feature in such fixtures. Bug-reporter language: "face missing after sewing", "sewer dropped face", "face silently lost", "sub-micron sliver".

## Reproducer recipe

A shell with one ADVANCED_FACE whose bounding wire encloses an area of (sewing_tol)² on a plane (e.g., CARTESIAN_POINTs spanning ~1e-6 in each direction), surrounded by larger faces.

## Expected kernel behavior

Always report dropped faces in a diagnostic list; configurable tolerance.

## Notes

Synonyms: "silent face loss", "sliver face drop".
